title: Config Commit Safeguard for Optimize Recommendation Cards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a transactional "safe commit" flow to the Optimize recommendation cards so customers can preview batching/caching configuration changes, run a dry-run evaluation, commit atomically, and have a verifiable audit chain with automatic rollback triggers if key SLOs regress. This ticket scopes the product requirements and UX flows for the console surface (cards, diff layer, commit modal, history) and defines acceptance criteria for dev and QA.
acceptance_criteria: Users can open a recommendation card and view a side-by-side computed diff between current runtime config and the recommended config (batch size, cache TTL, quantization profile).
A dry-run button submits the config to a sandboxed evaluator and returns an estimated token-cost delta and latency impact within 60s, surfaced in the diff panel.
Commit flow requires at least one safety check: either a signed approval (for high-impact changes) or an automated guardrail pass (SLO-preserving).
Commits are recorded as immutable audit entries with metadata (who, when, before/after snapshot, evaluation results) and visible in the Recommendation History tab.

Automatic rollback triggers if downstream observability detects >10% 95th percentile latency regression or >15% token-cost variance within the first 60 minutes; rollback action is recorded and notified to the owner.
All relevant operations have links to the execution logs, evaluation artifacts, and the supporting GitHub PR or deployment task.
design_notes: Avoid reusing the existing 'apply' modal — propose a separate 'Commit & Safeguard' modal that contains: diff view, dry-run, approval step, and an opt-in automatic rollback toggle.
Diff UI should highlight changed keys with in-line metric predictions (cost delta, latency delta, estimated savings) and color-coded risk badges (low/med/high).
Recommendation card will show a condensed one-line change summary and a secondary action to expand the full transactional flow.
Include a compact audit pill in the top-right of the card that opens the Recommendation History panel focused on that rule/config.
Mobility: design must work at ≤ 1024px width; stack diff under the card on narrow screens.
implementation_plan: API: extend optimize recommendations API to return recommended_snapshot, dry_run_endpoint, and risk_score (ENG-19812).
Backend: implement transactional commit object + audit ledger entries; add rollback worker that listens for telemetry triggers (ENG-20134).
Console: new Commit & Safeguard modal component, DiffRenderer, and Recommendation History panel — link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1234
Evaluator: dry-run harness to simulate batch/caching changes and return estimated unit economics; initial implementation on sandbox namespace only.
Feature flag behind 'optimize_safeguard_commit' for gradual rollout.
Telemetry: add 'recommendation.commit' and 'recommendation.rollback' events with metadata for downstream analytics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/optimize/recommendations
QA_checklist: Verify diff computation matches backend snapshots for at least 5 recommendation scenarios (short/long prompt, high/low token churn).
Dry-run returns consistent cost/latency estimates within 20% of observed values in sandbox runs.
Commit creates audit entry with before/after JSON snapshot and a linkable execution id.
Simulate SLO regression alert to confirm automatic rollback triggers and that notifications are sent to the commit owner.
Edge cases: conflicting concurrent commits (should fail with helpful error), expired approvals, and partial failures handled gracefully.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): enable feature flag for staging and Redwood internal teams. Solicit feedback from SRE and Platform PMs (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in via tenant flag for 5 pilot customers, monitor cost/latency impact and false positives for auto-rollback (4 weeks).
Phase 3 (public): gradual ramp to all tenants with default auto-rollback off; post-launch followups for default guardrail thresholds.
